Technology Services – CIO Domain

The Technology Services Team Works Directly With Private Equity Firms And Their Portfolio Companies To Drive Measurable Value Through Applied AI. Within The CIO Domain, Our Engagements Target The Enterprise IT Organization—infrastructure, Systems Of Record, Cybersecurity, And IT Operations—helping Portfolio Companies Embed AI To Reduce Cost, Strengthen Resilience, And Accelerate IT-enabled Business Outcomes. Specific Focus Areas Include

AI-enabled IT operating model design and enterprise architecture modernization
AIOps and intelligent IT operations: predictive incident management, automated remediation, and self-healing infrastructure
AI governance frameworks: AI-powered capabilities, model standards and lifecycle oversight, and AI capabilities risk management
Data governance: metadata and data classification, lineage and quality standards, access controls, retention and regulatory compliance oversight
Cloud infrastructure readiness for AI workload deployment (Azure, AWS, GCP)
Cybersecurity and AI risk: embedding AI-era controls across identity, access management, threat detection, and security operations
AI-embedded enterprise systems: Experience leveraging AI-native capabilities within core systems of record (SAP, Oracle, Workday, ServiceNow), including embedded copilots, intelligent automation, predictive workflows, and vendor AI roadmap evaluation
Data platform & BI transformation: Track record leading large-scale data platform modernization — including cloud and modern data platform architecture spanning hyperscalers and data-lake environments, enterprise data governance, and business intelligence enablement — to support AI-ready, insight-driven decision-making at scale
Establishment of FinOps for cloud and AI/ML operation capabilities and processes. IT cost optimization through intelligent automation of service desk, IT operations, and infrastructure management
End-to-end transformation execution, governance, and value tracking tied to IT financial targets

We align AI initiatives with investment theses, financial targets, and operational realities to ensure durable impact.

Role Overview

As a Director in the PEPI Technology Services AI team [CIO Domain], you will independently lead AI-driven value creation engagements across the private equity lifecycle, with a specific focus on the CIO organization of PE-backed portfolio companies. You own scope, workplan, client relationships, and financial outcomes end-to-end. You are the senior accountable leader on the engagement.

This role requires a practitioner who has operated inside or directly alongside CIO organizations—someone who has personally led IT transformations, managed vendors, governed AI deployments, or run enterprise technology programs—and who can translate that hands-on operating experience into rapid, credible impact within the compressed timelines of a PE holding period.

How You Will Contribute

Engagement Leadership & Client Ownership

Establish and champion the full engagement lifecycle: develop and roll-out playbooks for scoping, workplanning, team management, executive communications, and financial delivery against defined and productized AI targets
Serve as primary point of contact for portfolio company CIOs, IT leadership teams, and PE deal partners—building trusted advisor relationships that extend across the holding period
Lead cross-functional engagement teams spanning enterprise architecture, infrastructure, security, data, and IT operations
Drive executive-level workshops and steering committee presentations; translate complex IT findings into clear financial and operational narratives for PE audiences

AI Strategy, Diligence & Value Creation

Identify and prioritize AI use cases within the CIO domain mapped directly to EBITDA improvement, IT cost reduction, and risk mitigation
Lead AI-focused diligence workstreams: assess IT infrastructure maturity, data estate readiness, AI governance capabilities, cybersecurity posture, and ERP landscape to size value potential
Develop AI-enabled IT operating models and transformation roadmaps with specific financial targets, milestones, and accountability structures
Assess platform-native AI capabilities within ERP and ITSM systems and design adoption roadmaps within PE holding period constraints

Transformation Execution & Governance

Establish program governance, KPI frameworks, and value tracking tied to IT metrics: MTTR, SLA compliance, automation rate, incident deflection rate, and IT cost per user
Manage vendor relationships, managed service providers, and implementation partners across timelines, budgets, and execution risks
Redesign core IT processes to embed AI into operations: AIOps-driven incident triage, AI-assisted change management, automated compliance monitoring, and self-service IT portals
Align IT organizational structures and talent models to support AI-augmented operations

Practice Contribution

Support business development: contribute to proposals, respond to PE firm RFPs, and participate in client pitches
Mentor Senior Associates and Analysts; contribute to A&M's Technology Services methodology, tools, and accelerators for CIO domain engagements

Required Skills & Technology Fluency

Directors are expected to have demonstrated experience of successfully navigating, rolling out and governing implementations using the technologies below, not merely advised on them. Candidates should be able to speak to specific programs they have run, financial outcomes they delivered, and technical decisions they owned.

Enterprise-wide and Organizational IT AI Strategy & Governance

Design and operationalize enterprise Data and AI governance frameworks: AI powered capabilities and model risk policies, AI acceptable use standards, data lineage and usage controls, and model lifecycle management from deployment through decommission
Define and implement AI Center of Excellence (CoE) structures within IT organizations: staffing models, operating procedures, intake processes, and build-vs-buy evaluation frameworks
Conduct AI readiness assessments across IT domains—data quality, infrastructure elasticity, security posture, and organizational change capacity—and translate findings into investment-grade business cases
Establish KPIs and value tracking mechanisms for AI initiatives tied directly to EBITDA levers: IT cost per user, automation rate, mean time to resolve (MTTR), incident deflection rate, and SLA compliance
Navigate AI regulatory and compliance risk in enterprise IT contexts: GDPR/CCPA implications for AI data use, SOC 2 audit requirements for AI systems, and NIST AI RMF alignment

AIOps & Intelligent IT Operations

Deploy and tune AIOps platforms—Dynatrace, Datadog, Splunk ITSI, New Relic, IBM AIOps Insights, LogicMonitor—including alert correlation rules, anomaly detection thresholds, and automated remediation playbooks
Architect self-healing infrastructure pipelines: event-driven orchestration using ServiceNow ITOM, PagerDuty, xMatters, or equivalent—from anomaly detection through root cause analysis to auto-remediation
Configure and govern CMDB in ServiceNow or BMC Helix: CI relationships, dependency mapping, and service maps that underpin AIOps accuracy
Implement AI-enhanced service desk capabilities: conversational AI agents (ServiceNow Now Assist, Microsoft Copilot Studio), intelligent ticket classification and routing, and self-service deflection measurement
Deploy log intelligence and observability stacks: Splunk SPL for ML-based alerting, Elastic/ELK with anomaly detection, OpenTelemetry instrumentation standards, and distributed tracing across hybrid environments
Define and track IT operations metrics: MTTR, MTTD, change success rate, incident volume trends, and cost per ticket—with AI uplift quantified against baseline

Cloud Infrastructure & AI Workload Readiness

Architect cloud environments for AI workload deployment: GPU/TPU compute provisioning on Azure (ND-series, NC-series), AWS (P-series, Inf), and GCP (A100/H100 instances); cost governance for AI compute spend
Design and govern cloud landing zones and AI-ready infrastructure patterns: Azure AI Foundry, AWS SageMaker, Google Vertex AI—including network segmentation, private endpoints, and data residency controls
Implement and govern Infrastructure as Code at scale: Terraform modules, Ansible playbooks, Azure Bicep templates—with AI-assisted IaC generation and validation pipelines
Lead hybrid and multi-cloud architecture decisions: workload placement strategy, cloud cost optimization (FinOps), and AI platform consolidation within PE holding period capital constraints
Govern identity and access for AI systems: Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) conditional access policies, Okta workforce identity, CyberArk PAM for service account management, and zero-trust architecture for AI workloads

ERP & Systems of Record Transformation

Lead AI-augmentation programs on major ERP platforms: SAP S/4HANA with SAP Joule (AI copilot for finance, procurement, supply chain), Oracle Cloud ERP/HCM with Oracle Fusion AI, Workday Finance and HCM with Workday AI, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Copilot
Scope and govern ERP AI use cases within PE holding period constraints: automated journal entry creation, AI-assisted reconciliation, intelligent vendor invoice processing, predictive demand planning, and Copilot-driven financial close acceleration
Design and oversee data integration architectures connecting ERP systems to AI platforms: MuleSoft Anypoint, Azure Data Factory, Boomi, or equivalent—including data quality frameworks that gate AI model reliability
Assess and manage technical debt within ERP landscapes: identify customizations that block AI-native feature adoption and build remediation roadmaps tied to EBITDA targets
Lead master data governance initiatives required for AI accuracy: MDM platform selection (Informatica, Stibo, SAP MDG), data stewardship models, and golden record management

Cybersecurity & AI Risk Management

Design AI-era security architectures: zero-trust network access (ZTNA), microsegmentation, AI-augmented SIEM/SOAR platforms (Microsoft Sentinel, Splunk SOAR, Palo Alto XSIAM), and extended detection and response (XDR)
Govern AI-specific security risks: prompt injection controls, model access governance, training data poisoning prevention, and AI output monitoring for data exfiltration
Implement and assess against security frameworks: NIST CSF 2.0, CIS Controls v8, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II—with explicit mapping to AI system requirements
Lead identity security programs: privileged access management (CyberArk, BeyondTrust), identity governance and administration (SailPoint, Saviynt), and AI-assisted access certification
Oversee third-party and supply chain AI risk: vendor AI security assessments, AI model provenance, and contractual AI data usage controls

AI & Automation Platform Development

Architect and govern enterprise LLM deployments: Azure Ope

Alvarez & Marsal (A&M) is a global consulting firm with over 10,000 entrepreneurial, action and results-oriented professionals in over 40 countries. We take a hands-on approach to solving our clients' problems and assisting them in reaching their potential. Our culture celebrates independent thinkers and doers who positively impact our clients and shape our industry. The collaborative environment and engaging work—guided by A&M's core values of Integrity, Quality, Objectivity, Fun, Personal Reward, and Inclusive Diversity—are why our people love working at A&M.

A&M's Private Equity Performance Improvement Services (PEPI) practice focuses on serving upper middle market and large cap private equity firms who have engaged A&M to help improve operating results at their portfolio companies ($50M–$1B+ revenue range).

Our PEPI Services Include

IT / Product / Engineering [Technology Services]
CDD/Strategy
Interim Management
Merger Integration & Carve-outs
Rapid Results
Supply Chain
CFO Services

Technology Services – CIO Domain

The Technology Services Team Works Directly With Private Equity Firms And Their Portfolio Companies To Drive Measurable Value Through Applied AI. Within The CIO Domain, Our Engagements Target The Enterprise IT Organization—infrastructure, Systems Of Record, Cybersecurity, And IT Operations—helping Portfolio Companies Embed AI To Reduce Cost, Strengthen Resilience, And Accelerate IT-enabled Business Outcomes. Specific Focus Areas Include

AI-enabled IT operating model design and enterprise architecture modernization
AIOps and intelligent IT operations: predictive incident management, automated remediation, and self-healing infrastructure
AI governance frameworks: AI-powered capabilities, model standards and lifecycle oversight, and AI capabilities risk management
Data governance: metadata and data classification, lineage and quality standards, access controls, retention and regulatory compliance oversight
Cloud infrastructure readiness for AI workload deployment (Azure, AWS, GCP)
Cybersecurity and AI risk: embedding AI-era controls across identity, access management, threat detection, and security operations
AI-embedded enterprise systems: Experience leveraging AI-native capabilities within core systems of record (SAP, Oracle, Workday, ServiceNow), including embedded copilots, intelligent automation, predictive workflows, and vendor AI roadmap evaluation
Data platform & BI transformation: Track record leading large-scale data platform modernization — including cloud and modern data platform architecture spanning hyperscalers and data-lake environments, enterprise data governance, and business intelligence enablement — to support AI-ready, insight-driven decision-making at scale
Establishment of FinOps for cloud and AI/ML operation capabilities and processes. IT cost optimization through intelligent automation of service desk, IT operations, and infrastructure management
End-to-end transformation execution, governance, and value tracking tied to IT financial targets

We align AI initiatives with investment theses, financial targets, and operational realities to ensure durable impact.

Role Overview

As a Director in the PEPI Technology Services AI team [CIO Domain], you will independently lead AI-driven value creation engagements across the private equity lifecycle, with a specific focus on the CIO organization of PE-backed portfolio companies. You own scope, workplan, client relationships, and financial outcomes end-to-end. You are the senior accountable leader on the engagement.

This role requires a practitioner who has operated inside or directly alongside CIO organizations—someone who has personally led IT transformations, managed vendors, governed AI deployments, or run enterprise technology programs—and who can translate that hands-on operating experience into rapid, credible impact within the compressed timelines of a PE holding period.

How You Will Contribute

Engagement Leadership & Client Ownership

Establish and champion the full engagement lifecycle: develop and roll-out playbooks for scoping, workplanning, team management, executive communications, and financial delivery against defined and productized AI targets
Serve as primary point of contact for portfolio company CIOs, IT leadership teams, and PE deal partners—building trusted advisor relationships that extend across the holding period
Lead cross-functional engagement teams spanning enterprise architecture, infrastructure, security, data, and IT operations
Drive executive-level workshops and steering committee presentations; translate complex IT findings into clear financial and operational narratives for PE audiences

AI Strategy, Diligence & Value Creation

Identify and prioritize AI use cases within the CIO domain mapped directly to EBITDA improvement, IT cost reduction, and risk mitigation
Lead AI-focused diligence workstreams: assess IT infrastructure maturity, data estate readiness, AI governance capabilities, cybersecurity posture, and ERP landscape to size value potential
Develop AI-enabled IT operating models and transformation roadmaps with specific financial targets, milestones, and accountability structures
Assess platform-native AI capabilities within ERP and ITSM systems and design adoption roadmaps within PE holding period constraints

Transformation Execution & Governance

Establish program governance, KPI frameworks, and value tracking tied to IT metrics: MTTR, SLA compliance, automation rate, incident deflection rate, and IT cost per user
Manage vendor relationships, managed service providers, and implementation partners across timelines, budgets, and execution risks
Redesign core IT processes to embed AI into operations: AIOps-driven incident triage, AI-assisted change management, automated compliance monitoring, and self-service IT portals
Align IT organizational structures and talent models to support AI-augmented operations

Practice Contribution

Support business development: contribute to proposals, respond to PE firm RFPs, and participate in client pitches
Mentor Senior Associates and Analysts; contribute to A&M's Technology Services methodology, tools, and accelerators for CIO domain engagements

Required Skills & Technology Fluency

Directors are expected to have demonstrated experience of successfully navigating, rolling out and governing implementations using the technologies below, not merely advised on them. Candidates should be able to speak to specific programs they have run, financial outcomes they delivered, and technical decisions they owned.

Enterprise-wide and Organizational IT AI Strategy & Governance

Design and operationalize enterprise Data and AI governance frameworks: AI powered capabilities and model risk policies, AI acceptable use standards, data lineage and usage controls, and model lifecycle management from deployment through decommission
Define and implement AI Center of Excellence (CoE) structures within IT organizations: staffing models, operating procedures, intake processes, and build-vs-buy evaluation frameworks
Conduct AI readiness assessments across IT domains—data quality, infrastructure elasticity, security posture, and organizational change capacity—and translate findings into investment-grade business cases
Establish KPIs and value tracking mechanisms for AI initiatives tied directly to EBITDA levers: IT cost per user, automation rate, mean time to resolve (MTTR), incident deflection rate, and SLA compliance
Navigate AI regulatory and compliance risk in enterprise IT contexts: GDPR/CCPA implications for AI data use, SOC 2 audit requirements for AI systems, and NIST AI RMF alignment

AIOps & Intelligent IT Operations

Deploy and tune AIOps platforms—Dynatrace, Datadog, Splunk ITSI, New Relic, IBM AIOps Insights, LogicMonitor—including alert correlation rules, anomaly detection thresholds, and automated remediation playbooks
Architect self-healing infrastructure pipelines: event-driven orchestration using ServiceNow ITOM, PagerDuty, xMatters, or equivalent—from anomaly detection through root cause analysis to auto-remediation
Configure and govern CMDB in ServiceNow or BMC Helix: CI relationships, dependency mapping, and service maps that underpin AIOps accuracy
Implement AI-enhanced service desk capabilities: conversational AI agents (ServiceNow Now Assist, Microsoft Copilot Studio), intelligent ticket classification and routing, and self-service deflection measurement
Deploy log intelligence and observability stacks: Splunk SPL for ML-based alerting, Elastic/ELK with anomaly detection, OpenTelemetry instrumentation standards, and distributed tracing across hybrid environments
Define and track IT operations metrics: MTTR, MTTD, change success rate, incident volume trends, and cost per ticket—with AI uplift quantified against baseline

Cloud Infrastructure & AI Workload Readiness

Architect cloud environments for AI workload deployment: GPU/TPU compute provisioning on Azure (ND-series, NC-series), AWS (P-series, Inf), and GCP (A100/H100 instances); cost governance for AI compute spend
Design and govern cloud landing zones and AI-ready infrastructure patterns: Azure AI Foundry, AWS SageMaker, Google Vertex AI—including network segmentation, private endpoints, and data residency controls
Implement and govern Infrastructure as Code at scale: Terraform modules, Ansible playbooks, Azure Bicep templates—with AI-assisted IaC generation and validation pipelines
Lead hybrid and multi-cloud architecture decisions: workload placement strategy, cloud cost optimization (FinOps), and AI platform consolidation within PE holding period capital constraints
Govern identity and access for AI systems: Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) conditional access policies, Okta workforce identity, CyberArk PAM for service account management, and zero-trust architecture for AI workloads

ERP & Systems of Record Transformation

Lead AI-augmentation programs on major ERP platforms: SAP S/4HANA with SAP Joule (AI copilot for finance, procurement, supply chain), Oracle Cloud ERP/HCM with Oracle Fusion AI, Workday Finance and HCM with Workday AI, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Copilot
Scope and govern ERP AI use cases within PE holding period constraints: automated journal entry creation, AI-assisted reconciliation, intelligent vendor invoice processing, predictive demand planning, and Copilot-driven financial close acceleration
Design and oversee data integration architectures connecting ERP systems to AI platforms: MuleSoft Anypoint, Azure Data Factory, Boomi, or equivalent—including data quality frameworks that gate AI model reliability
Assess and manage technical debt within ERP landscapes: identify customizations that block AI-native feature adoption and build remediation roadmaps tied to EBITDA targets
Lead master data governance initiatives required for AI accuracy: MDM platform selection (Informatica, Stibo, SAP MDG), data stewardship models, and golden record management

Cybersecurity & AI Risk Management

Design AI-era security architectures: zero-trust network access (ZTNA), microsegmentation, AI-augmented SIEM/SOAR platforms (Microsoft Sentinel, Splunk SOAR, Palo Alto XSIAM), and extended detection and response (XDR)
Govern AI-specific security risks: prompt injection controls, model access governance, training data poisoning prevention, and AI output monitoring for data exfiltration
Implement and assess against security frameworks: NIST CSF 2.0, CIS Controls v8, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II—with explicit mapping to AI system requirements
Lead identity security programs: privileged access management (CyberArk, BeyondTrust), identity governance and administration (SailPoint, Saviynt), and AI-assisted access certification
Oversee third-party and supply chain AI risk: vendor AI security assessments, AI model provenance, and contractual AI data usage controls

AI & Automation Platform Development

Architect and govern enterprise LLM deployments: Azure Ope

new_jobs.title: Director, Infrastructure Engineering
new_jobs.description:
Company Overview

At Enlyte, we combine innovative technology, clinical expertise, and human compassion to help people recover after workplace injuries or auto accidents. We support their journey back to health and wellness through our industry-leading solutions and services. Whether you're supporting a Fortune 500 client or a local business, developing cutting-edge technology, or providing clinical services you'll work alongside dedicated professionals who share your commitment to excellence and make a meaningful impact. Join us in fueling our mission to protect dreams and restore lives, while building your career in an environment that values collaboration, innovation, and personal growth.

Be part of a team that makes a real difference.

Job Description

This is a full-time remote position that can be located anywhere in the U.S

The Director, Infrastructure Engineering is responsible for leading Enlyte's infrastructure engineering organization, encompassing cloud engineering, data center infrastructure, network and firewall management, and operating systems (Windows/Linux). This role owns the strategic evolution from on-premises data centers to multi-cloud (AWS & Azure), including the decommissioning of legacy facilities, cloud migration infrastructure readiness, and establishment of cloud-native network capabilties.

The role holds direct accountability for vendor and cloud consumption portfolio, manages engineers, and requires cross-functional program governance across multiple organizational boundaries. This leader will drive complex, multi-year infrastructure transformation while maintaining operational excellence for production systems and ensuring the organization successfully transitions to a product delivery model.

Reporting Relationship: Reports to Vice President, Technology Engineering & Platforms

Key Responsibilities

Lead the infrastructure engineering function including cloud engineering, compute/server, network, OS/Linux, and firewall management
Define and execute the data center exit strategy with complete plans, timelines, risk assessments, cost models, and cross-functional governance across Server, Resiliency, PMO, Managed Services, Facilities, and Finance
Drive the enterprise network architecture strategy for multi-cloud environments, including SD-WAN, VPN, east-west inspection, load balancing, and hybrid connectivity
Manage the enterprise firewall platform (physical and cloud-native NGFW), including vendor lifecycle management, capacity planning, patching, and renewal strategy
Direct OS/compute engineering operations including Linux/Windows patching strategy, and server lifecycle management
Manage a portfolio of strategic vendor relationships, including commercial negotiations, SLA governance, renewal strategy, and RFP development
Drive network and infrastructure readiness for cloud migration programs, including VPN cutover governance, load testing, and production traffic transition
Lead major incident response for infrastructure; own PIR/AAR process and drive systemic availability improvements
Build and develop a high-performing infrastructure engineering team; identify skill gaps, manage performance, develop talent pipelines, and leverage managed services staff augmentation
Ensure infrastructure architecture standards maximize efficiency, support platform compatibility, and enable the broader organizational transition to a product/service delivery model
Provide regular, transparent reporting on infrastructure program status, cloud spend, vendor portfolio health, and risk posture to executive leadership

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Technology, Engineering, or related field, or equivalent experience
12+ years of experience in infrastructure engineering, cloud engineering, or IT operations with progressive leadership responsibility
Demonstrated experience leading data center migrations, cloud transformations, or decommissioning programs
Expertise in cloud architecture (AWS, Azure) including infrastructure-as-code, landing zones, networking, and cost management
Strong knowledge of enterprise network architecture (SD-WAN, MPLS, VPN, cloud networking, load balancing)
Experience with firewall platforms (NGFW, cloud-native firewalls) and network security fundamentals
Track record of cross-functional program leadership across multiple organizational boundaries
People leadership: building and managing teams of 10+, talent development, and performance management
Strong communication and stakeholder management skills with ability to influence senior technology leaders

Preferred Qualifications

Industry certifications (AWS Solutions Architect Professional, CCNP/CCIE, Azure Solutions Architect, or equivalent)
Experience in insurance, claims, or financial services technology environments
Experience managing managed services relationships (outsourced infrastructure operations, NOC oversight)
Experience with organizational transformation from project-based to product/service delivery models
Experience with infrastructure divestiture planning (lease exits, hardware disposition, contract termination)
Experience with cloud cost management and FinOps practices
Familiarity with Linux/UNIX administration, middleware platforms (JBoss, WebLogic), and server lifecycle management

Key Competencies

Strategic thinking and multi-year infrastructure planning
Vendor management and commercial negotiation
Cross-functional influence without direct authority
Program governance and executive communication
Decision-making under ambiguity and competing priorities
Organizational leadership and talent development
Incident management and operational resilience
Technical depth balanced with business acumen

Benefits

We’re committed to supporting your ultimate well-being through our total compensation package offerings that support your health, wealth and self. These offerings include Medical, Dental, Vision, Health Savings Accounts / Flexible Spending Accounts, Life and AD&D Insurance, 401(k), Tuition Reimbursement, and an array of resources that encourage a lifetime of healthier living. Benefits eligibility may differ depending on full-time or part-time status. Compensation depends on the applicable US geographic market. The expected base pay for this position ranges from $130,796 - $185,000 annually, and will be based on a number of additional factors including skills, experience, and education.

The Company is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, status as a protected veteran, among other things, or status as a qualified individual with disability.

Don’t meet every single requirement? Studies have shown that women and underrepresented minorities are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single qualification. We are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

new_jobs.title: Sr. Manager, Software Engineering
new_jobs.description:
Care.com is a consumer tech company with heart. We’re on a mission to solve a human challenge we all face: finding great care for the ones we love. We’re moms and dads and pet parents. We have parents and grandparents so we understand that everyone, at some point in their lives, could use a helping hand. Our culture and our products reflect that.

Job Description

We are seeking a highly motivated Senior Engineering Manager to lead our payments engineering team. You will manage a high-performing, agile team of engineers dedicated to building and scaling our payments ecosystem. You will be responsible for the end-to-end architecture, development, and maintenance of our financial technology platform, processing millions of high-volume financial transactions, subscriptions, and payouts for families and caregivers securely and reliably.

Lead a focused, agile team of engineers responsible for the end-to-end management of our payments platform.
Lead the ongoing optimization and advancement of our Stripe-based payment infrastructure to ensure high performance and scalability, following the successful migration from our legacy Vantiv systems.
Design, build, and maintain high-volume, fault-tolerant, and secure payment processing services capable of handling massive transactional throughput.
Oversee the integration and optimization of diverse payment methods, including Apple Pay, Google Pay, and P2P payment solutions, ensuring scalability and strict regulatory compliance.
Partner with Product, Finance, and Compliance stakeholders to translate complex business requirements into technical solutions that ensure regulatory alignment and financial integrity.
Partner with architects to decompose legacy platform components and transition core payment features into a clean, event-driven architecture.
Champion engineering best practices—including observability, testing, performance, scalability, and security across the payments domain.
Mentor and guide the professional and technical development of your team, fostering a culture of high-quality engineering, collaborative problem-solving, and continuous improvement.
Oversee on-call practices, SLAs, and incident management to maintain platform resilience and availability.

Qualifications

8+ years of professional engineering experience.
3+ years of experience leading a team (Engineering Manager or Team Lead).
Deep experience building and scaling payments platforms (Stripe, PayPal, ApplePay, ACH), gateway integrations (specifically Stripe) and a strong understanding of navigating legacy payment system migrations (e.g., Vantiv) to support our current architecture.

About the company:
Hiring for Pakistan’s premier credit bureau organisation.

Job Overview:

The Head of IT is responsible for the overall leadership, strategy, governance, security, reliability, and performance of the organization's technology environment.

Job Responsibilities:

IT Infrastructure / IT Operations Team
Software Development Team
Software Quality Assurance (SQA) Team
Other technology functions as assigned
Database Management & Data Infrastructure
The Head of IT will have overall responsibility for the organization's database environment, ensuring the availability, performance, security, integrity, and recoverability of all critical databases.

Key Responsibilities

Oversee the Database Administration (DBA) function and database infrastructure.
Ensure high availability, reliability and optimal performance of production databases.
Establish standards for database architecture, configuration, maintenance and capacity planning.
Ensure effective database backup, restoration, replication and disaster recovery mechanisms.
Ensure databases are appropriately integrated into the organization's Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) framework.
Establish appropriate database security, access controls, privileges and segregation of duties.
Ensure data integrity, consistency and appropriate controls over critical organizational data.
Oversee database patching, upgrades, version management and lifecycle planning.
Establish and monitor database maintenance, health checks and preventive management processes.
Work closely with Software Development and SQA teams to ensure efficient database design, queries, stored procedures and application performance.
Review and approve database changes associated with major application releases.
Ensure appropriate development, testing and production database environments are maintained.
Establish standards for database documentation, change management and configuration management.
Monitor and manage database-related incidents and ensure timely resolution.
Ensure database capacity planning is aligned with business growth and future technology requirements.
Coordinate database-related activities with Infrastructure, Development, SQA, Cybersecurity, and business teams.
Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory, information security, and data protection requirements.

IT Strategy & Leadership

Develop and implement the organization's IT strategy in alignment with business objectives.
Establish technology roadmaps covering infrastructure, applications, software development, cybersecurity and digital transformation.
Lead the IT function and establish appropriate structures, processes, policies, and governance mechanisms.
Advise senior management on technology investments, emerging technologies, risks and opportunities.
Prepare and manage the annual IT budget and ensure effective utilization of technology resources.
Develop technology standards, architecture principles and IT policies.

Software Development

Lead and oversee the Software Development function and ensure timely delivery of business applications and technology solutions.
Establish software development methodologies, standards and coding practices.
Ensure proper requirement gathering, solution design, development, documentation and deployment processes.
Establish appropriate SDLC, Agile/Scrum or other development frameworks based on organizational requirements.
Ensure software projects are delivered within agreed scope, timelines, quality standards and budgets.
Promote scalable, maintainable and secure application architecture.
Ensure proper version control, source-code management, release management and documentation.
Oversee integration of internal systems with external platforms, APIs and third-party applications.
Drive modernization of legacy applications where required.

Software Quality Assurance (SQA)

Lead the SQA function and establish a robust software quality framework.
Ensure appropriate testing is conducted throughout the Software Development Life Cycle.
Establish standards for functional, regression, integration, performance, security, and user acceptance testing.
Ensure test plans, test cases, test scenarios and defect management processes are properly maintained.
Monitor software defect rates, severity, resolution timelines and recurring defects.
Ensure adequate testing before production releases.
Promote automation of repetitive and regression testing where commercially and technically appropriate.
Establish quality gates and release criteria for critical applications.
Work closely with Development, Business and IT Operations teams to improve overall software quality.

IT Infrastructure & Operations

Oversee IT infrastructure including servers, networks, data centers, cloud platforms, storage, end-user computing and communication systems.
Ensure high availability, reliability and performance of critical IT services.
Establish appropriate monitoring, preventive maintenance and capacity management processes.
Ensure effective incident, problem, change and service management.
Maintain appropriate disaster recovery and business continuity arrangements.
Ensure defined RTO/RPO requirements are implemented and regularly tested.
Manage IT vendors, service providers and technology partners.

Cybersecurity & Information Security

Ensure protection of organizational systems, applications, networks and data.
Oversee vulnerability management, security monitoring, access controls and security assessments.
Ensure appropriate security controls are incorporated into software development and infrastructure.
Coordinate response to cybersecurity incidents and ensure timely remediation.
Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory and industry requirements.

IT Governance, Risk & Compliance

Establish IT governance frameworks, policies, procedures, and controls.
Ensure technology operations comply with applicable laws, regulations, organizational policies and regulatory requirements.
Identify and manage technology-related risks.
Maintain appropriate IT documentation, inventories, policies and control frameworks.
Support internal and external audits and ensure timely closure of audit observations.
Ensure appropriate segregation of duties and technology controls.

Project & Change Management

Oversee major IT and software development projects from initiation through implementation.
Establish project priorities based on business value, risk, and available resources.
Monitor project scope, timelines, budgets, dependencies and risks.
Ensure proper change management and stakeholder communication.
Ensure post-implementation reviews are conducted for major technology projects.

Team Leadership & Development

Lead, mentor and develop IT, Software Development and SQA teams.
Establish clear objectives, KPIs and accountability for technology teams.
Identify skills gaps and develop appropriate training and succession plans.
Build a culture of innovation, accountability, quality and continuous improvement.
Ensure effective resource planning and optimal utilization of IT personnel.

Database Management & Data Infrastructure

Oversee the Database Administration (DBA) function and database infrastructure.
Ensure high availability, reliability, and optimal performance of production databases.
Establish standards for database architecture, configuration, maintenance and capacity planning.
Ensure effective database backup, restoration, replication and disaster recovery mechanisms.
Ensure databases are appropriately integrated into the organization's Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) framework.
Monitor database performance, capacity, availability and resource utilization.
Establish appropriate database security, access controls, privileges and segregation of duties.
Oversee database patching, upgrades, version management and lifecycle planning.
Establish and monitor database maintenance, health checks and preventive management processes.
Ensure appropriate database monitoring and alerting mechanisms are in place.

delivery of approved automation/digital initiatives.

maintaining agreed availability and successful DR capability.

timely delivery of applications with minimal production defects.
Cybersecurity & Regulatory Compliance –
maintaining required security and compliance standards.

managing technology expenditure within approved budget while identifying efficiencies.

ensuring IT solutions effectively support business requirements.

IT strategy and technology roadmap
IT infrastructure and operations

Cybersecurity and IT risk

Technology projects

new_jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager - Agentic Analytics
new_jobs.description:
At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.

At the center of the data cloud is the Snowflake Database Engineering team. We are responsible for building the core query engine used to process the massive amounts of diverse data managed by our customers. A core part of the Database Engineering group is the Query Language team which is responsible for designing, developing, and maintaining core SQL features, including advanced analytics, scripting, and the developer experience.

We are seeking a Senior Engineering Manager
to own and drive the effort to build core database capabilities to serve agentic workloads. You'll set the technical direction, build and grow the team behind it, and shape how the core engine and the SQL language evolve to serve this new class of workload. It's a rare chance to lead a foundational bet at the exact moment the industry is racing to solve it, with the scale, customer base, and platform to make your work matter to millions of queries a day. If you want your fingerprints on how the world's data platforms adapt to the age of AI agents, this is one of the best seats in the industry.

AS A SENIOR ENGINEERING MANAGER AT SNOWFLAKE, YOU WILL BE EXPECTED TO:

Drive the evolution of core database and SQL capabilities to serve emerging AI and agentic workloads alongside traditional analytics
Lead and grow a team of talented engineers in the design, development, and support of a highly-parallel and fault-tolerant SQL database system
Support engineers in their career development by providing clear feedback and developing engineering leaders
Translate product requirements into engineering work for your team
Collaborate with other local and global teams and leaders across the Engineering and Product Management organizations
Use your strong foundation as a technical leader to reliably deliver on complex projects while keeping the quality bar high
Foster a culture of creativity and innovation while also promoting practical decision-making

OUR IDEAL CANDIDATE WILL HAVE:

10+ years of experience building and operating large-scale systems (distributed systems, databases, or cloud services)
5+ years of experience leading teams to build database system internals (experience leading managers is a strong plus)
Rock solid engineering fundamentals; query processing experience is highly preferred but not required
Exposure to AI, ML, or agent-driven workloads and how they consume data platforms
A track record of recruiting and leading technical teams in a demanding talent market
Proven experience authoring roadmap documents, project plans, and RCAs
Strong problem solving skills and excellent interpersonal communication skills

BONUS POINTS FOR EXPERIENCE WITH THE FOLLOWING:

Background in database internals or large-scale data processing systems, e.g., Hadoop, Spark, etc.
Prior experience running SQL database engineering teams
Proven experience authoring product roadmaps, preparing and reviewing project design and test plan documents, and managing projects with JIRA

WHY BE A SENIOR ENGINEERING MANAGER FOR DATABASE ENGINEERING AT SNOWFLAKE?

This is an excellent opportunity to:

Lead and grow an exceptional team of industry veterans and rising stars building the industry-leading data management system that customers love
Shape how the core database serves the next generation of AI and agentic workloads, a problem the whole industry is racing to solve
Take charge of your own career. This role will push you to grow, both technically and as a team leader
Learn at scale as you and your team deliver essential components of a highly distributed, robust, and secure enterprise SaaS platform that services thousands of customers and more than a billion complex queries every day

Every Snowflake employee is expected to follow the company’s confidentiality and security standards for handling sensitive data. Snowflake employees must abide by the company’s data security plan as an essential part of their duties. It is every employee's duty to keep customer information secure and confidential.

Snowflake is growing fast, and we’re scaling our team to help enable and accelerate our growth. We are looking for people who share our values, challenge ordinary thinking, and push the pace of innovation while building a future for themselves and Snowflake.

How do you want to make your impact?

For jobs located in the United States, please visit the job posting on the Snowflake Careers Site for salary and benefits information: careers.snowflake.com

The estimated base salary range for this role is $264,000 - $379,500.
Additionally, this role is eligible to participate in Snowflake’s bonus and equity plan.

The successful candidate’s starting salary will be determined based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location. This role is also eligible for a competitive benefits package that includes: medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance; 401(k) retirement plan; flexible spending & health savings account; at least 12 paid holidays; paid time off; parental leave; employee assistance program; and other company benefits.
